dossier.public_summary: The dip reported every 14 days changes strongly between sectors and between individual transits, and odd and even events have very different depths. A star 17 arcseconds away could produce the signal with a stellar eclipse, but TESS cannot localize it. The pattern matches an eclipsing binary or blended binary better than a single planet.

reasons.why: Odd and even depths differ by 4.03 sigma with depth_ratio 1.8; sector_oe_max_sigma 7.511 and sector_oe_sectors_over_3 1 in one sector. Strong odd/even difference is positive evidence for an eclipsing binary at twice the period (14d), not a planet.

Depth changes dramatically sector-to-sector: 1195, 2068, 3368, 762 ppm. sector_depths_by_source verdict changes_within_a_source with p_constant 3.7149818182558763e-06 even within QLP, so not just aperture/curation. Inconsistent depth across an ephemeris favors blend/binary variability over a planet.

Individual transit depths are not consistent (chi2 97.7 dof 5) with outliers at -7.1 sigma (3 ppm) and +4.7 sigma (3368 ppm); top 3 transits carry 88% of signal, consistent with a few eclipses/ble map of a NEB rather than repeating planetary transits.

Centroid is inconclusive with no sector difference image, so on-target is not established. There are 2 stars within 1 pixel and 60 that could cause the dip, with closest at 16.7 arcsec needing 12% eclipse. No on-target confirmation combined with variable depth makes off-target/blend likely.
Planet rank in bottom decile of known planets, consistent with a low planet-like likelihood given the above binary/blend signs.
